newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GERLING UNIT EYES GROWTH IN CREDIT INSURANCE.
newsitem.headline: GERLING UNIT EYES GROWTH IN CREDIT INSURANCE.

text.p: Belgium's Gerling Namur credit insurance company, a unit of Germany's Gerling Group, said on Tuesday it aimed to raise revenues by 10 percent a year between now and 1999, while lifting return on equity to around 12 from six percent.

At a news conference, Gerling Namur, formerly known as Namur-Assurances du Credit, said it aimed also to take full control of French credit insurer Sacren this year. At present, Namur owns 60 percent of Sacren, a stake it bought last year from French insurers GAN and Mutuelle du Mans.
"The price has been agreed," Namur chief executive officer Guy Lammens said. He declined to give financial details.
Namur consolidated 1996 net profit nearly doubled to 131 million francs from 76 million francs. Premium income rose 29 percent to 6.62 billion francs.

Namur Chairman and Gerling representative Bernd Meyer said that, together with Namur, Gerling's specialist credit insurance unit GKS now saw good chances of becoming at least number two on all its core markets in the coming years.
"We will also expect to be number two worldwide within two years," he said.
At present, GKS/Gerling Namur ranks third worldwide in terms of premium income behind French group SFAC and Germany's state backed Hermes group, Meyer said.
Gerling is 30 percent held by Deutsche Bank and 70 percent by the founding Gerling family.
